transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know! I do have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using any eye drops or gels you were using before your operation for dry eyes, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're unsure about the specific product you have, I'd recommend checking with your GP or pharmacist to confirm it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s helpful, thank you! Here's another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I have one more question: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about a week ago, so it sounds like I'm still within the normal range. I appreciate all the information. I don't have any more questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's wonderful! I'm glad I could help, and it sounds like you're progressing well.

Just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care and wishing you a smooth recovery.

verdict.label: pass
